outcome: Fix the PR #6 review findings: a close-name rewrite is offered only when the call resolves under that name and the name is not an engine function of its own, min is offered only where it applies, an aggregate where a scalar is expected is explained, and a two-argument datediff names the unit-first form.
criteria: strptime and isnull(x, y) are not renamed; any and last are not one value per group; any_value on a boolean field and any are explained without a rewrite; first in a derive is explained as an aggregate; datediff(start, end) names date_diff('day', start, end); a test covers each and the full suite passes.

note: renamed_function in typing.py tries the close name with the call's arguments and types and skips NOT_A_MISSPELLING (strptime, ltrim, rtrim); the resolver attaches details.renamed only then. The aggregate refusal carries min_applies from the field's type. One new test plus additions to an existing one fail without the fix; 395 passed.
